passage:
The rain had trapped everyone under the bus shelter, and the bus was late. Ayesha stared at her friend Rashmi's new fringe, which stood straight up like a small broom. "You look like a coconut with a mohawk!" said Ayesha, laughing.
"Well, you look like an owl," Rashmi shot back, "when you wear your specs and blink."
They both burst out laughing. Ayesha's face turned serious for a second. "Too much? Tell me if it's too much."
"No, it's funny," said Rashmi, patting the fringe. "But if you say it a fifth time, I'll say stop."
"Deal."

qa.q: What did Ayesha say Rashmi looked like?
qa.a: A coconut with a mohawk.

qa.q: What was Ayesha feeling when asking "Too much? Tell me if it's too much"?
qa.a: Caring and a little concerned about crossing a line, even though both had been laughing.

qa.q: What makes this teasing friendly rather than hurtful?
qa.a: Both laugh and both tease, and Ayesha checks in while Rashmi says how far it can go and that stop would work.

qa.q: How might Rashmi feel about the teasing about the fringe?
qa.a: Amused and comfortable, since Rashmi teased back, patted the fringe and set a light limit.

grounding: Ayesha and Rashmi tease each other about a haircut and laugh together, both aware it is affectionate and either can say stop.

passage:
Omkar came back from the barber with a haircut so short it showed the pale skin above the ears. His friend Harsha met him at the colony gate and snorted. "You look like a peeled potato!"
Omkar laughed and rubbed the head. "You should talk. Your hairband is bigger than your head!"
"It's a scientific hairband," said Harsha.
For a while they carried on like that, each trying to outdo the other. Then Omkar said, "Okay, that's enough about my head now."
"Okay," said Harsha, and immediately asked, "Race to the swings?" Omkar was already running.

qa.q: What did Harsha call Omkar's haircut?
qa.a: A peeled potato.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling when saying "Okay, that's enough about my head now"?
qa.a: Omkar had enjoyed the fun but was a bit tired of jokes about the head, and wanted the subject changed.

qa.q: What made the ending of the teasing go well?
qa.a: Omkar said stop clearly and lightly, and Harsha respected it at once by suggesting a race to the swings.

qa.q: How might Harsha feel after being told "that's enough"?
qa.a: Fine and unbothered, since Harsha said okay right away and changed the game, showing that the teasing was friendly and that Harsha could stop.

grounding: Omkar and Harsha tease each other about a haircut and laugh, and one says enough and the other stops.

passage: At the school gate on Monday, Arohi pulled off her cap. Her long hair was gone, cut short over the weekend. Swati gasped. "You look like a mushroom!" Arohi laughed. "A very stylish mushroom." "A mushroom with earrings!" Swati was giggling so hard she had to hold the gate. Arohi grinned and spun around. In the corridor, their friend Nimmi said, "Mushroom-head!" Arohi paused. "Okay, only Swati gets to say mushroom. You can say stylish." Nimmi laughed. "Stylish, then." Swati linked arms with her. "I actually love it, you know." Arohi smiled. "I know."

qa.q: What did Swati say Arohi looked like?
qa.a: A mushroom.

qa.q: How did Arohi feel about Swati's teasing?
qa.a: She felt amused and relaxed, laughing and joking back because she knew it was affectionate.

qa.q: What shows this teasing stayed friendly?
qa.a: Both girls laughed, Arohi could set a limit with Nimmi and be listened to, and Swati said she actually loved the haircut.

qa.q: How might Nimmi have felt when Arohi set the limit?
qa.a: Nimmi seemed fine with it, laughing and switching to 'stylish' without feeling hurt.

grounding: Shows friends teasing each other about a haircut and laughing together, with everyone enjoying it and free to say stop.

passage:
Monday: Akash came to class with a buzz cut. Gurleen ran her hand over it. "Hedgehog!" Akash laughed and made hedgehog noises. They both cracked up.
Wednesday: Gurleen got braces. Akash grinned. "Metal mouth!" Gurleen's smile faded a little. "Not the braces. They hurt." Akash stopped at once. "Sorry. No braces jokes." "But hedgehog's still allowed," she said.
Friday: Akash's hair was a bit longer. "Baby hedgehog," Gurleen said. Akash laughed and poked her pencil. "Worst nickname ever." They were still giggling when the bell rang.

qa.q: What did Gurleen call Akash's buzz cut?
qa.a: Hedgehog.

qa.q: What was Gurleen feeling when Akash said 'Metal mouth'?
qa.a: She felt hurt and uncomfortable, because the braces were painful.

qa.q: What did Akash do right on Wednesday?
qa.a: Akash stopped at once and apologised when Gurleen said 'not the braces', respecting her limit.

qa.q: How did the teasing feel for both of them by Friday?
qa.a: It felt fun and friendly again, with Akash and Gurleen both giggling.

grounding: Shows two friends teasing affectionately about a haircut, where either can say stop and the other listens.

passage:
"Yogesh, you're sulking because Rahul called your haircut a helmet?" said Zubin dadaji, chuckling. "Let me tell you about my friend Homi. When we were ten, I had ears that stuck out like cup handles. Homi called me 'Teacup'. And I called him 'Beanpole', because he was so tall and thin. We laughed ourselves silly every day.
Once, when my grandmother died, Homi said 'Teacup' at the funeral lunch, and I said, 'Not today, Homi.' He went red and said, 'Sorry, yaar.' He never said it on a sad day again.
That's how you know teasing is friendly. You both enjoy it, and either one can say stop, and the other stops. Now, do you and Rahul laugh together, or only one of you?"

qa.q: What did Homi call Zubin dadaji?
qa.a: Teacup.

qa.q: How did young Zubin feel at the funeral lunch when Homi said 'Teacup'?
qa.a: He felt hurt and sad, because it was the wrong day for teasing.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Zubin dadaji's story?
qa.a: Saying 'Not today, Homi' at the funeral lunch, when Homi apologised and never used the nickname on a sad day again.

qa.q: How might Homi have felt when Zubin said 'Not today'?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and sorry, going red and apologising.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling friendly teasing where both friends enjoyed it and either could say stop.

passage: Class photo day, eight minutes to the photographer, and Vaibhav's new haircut stood straight up at the back like a rooster's comb. Hrithik spotted it at the bus stop and gasped. "Bro. Did a goat cut your hair?" Vaibhav grinned. "A goat with scissors. Very talented goat." They both howled. Hrithik licked his palm and tried to flatten it; it sprang straight back up. "Cock-a-doodle-doo," he said, and Vaibhav crowed back. Then Vaibhav added, half serious, "Okay, but if anyone else says rooster in the photo line, I'll be annoyed." "Then only I'm allowed," Hrithik said. "Deal?" "Deal." In the photo both of them are grinning, and the comb is clearly visible.

qa.q: What did Hrithik use to try to flatten the hair?
qa.a: He used his licked palm.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel about Hrithik's goat joke?
qa.a: He felt amused and comfortable 😄 grinning and adding his own joke about a talented goat.

qa.q: What kept the teasing friendly?
qa.a: Both of them were laughing, and Vaibhav could say where his limit was, which Hrithik agreed to at once.

qa.q: What would change if other classmates started saying "rooster" in the photo line?
qa.a: Vaibhav said he'd be annoyed, so from others it could feel like being mocked instead of fun shared with a friend.

grounding: Shows two friends teasing each other about a haircut, both enjoying it and able to set a limit.
